book.title: Mahmud Kashgari: The Oldest Turkish Dictionary (A1)

pages.title: A Very Old Dictionary
pages.content:
Mahmud Kashgari wrote a very old book. It is called Dîvânu Lugâti’t-Türk. It is the oldest dictionary of the Turkish language. He started to write it in 1072 and finished it in 1074. In 1077, he gave it to the Caliph in Baghdad.

Mahmud wrote the book in Arabic. He wanted to teach Turkish to Arab people. He also wanted to show everybody something: Turkish is a rich and beautiful language. Today, there is only one copy of the book. It is in Istanbul, in the Millet Library.

vocabulary.definition: A book with words and their meanings.
The leader of the Muslims.
One book of many same books.

pages.title: Who Was Mahmud?
pages.content:
Mahmud was born in 1008 in Barsgan. Today, Barsgan is in Kyrgyzstan. His family was from the Karakhanids. It was an important family.

He lived in Kashgar for many years and died there in 1105. Kashgar is a very old city in East Turkestan. That is why people call him Kashgari, “the man from Kashgar”. In his book, Mahmud also writes about himself. He speaks Turkish very well. He is also very good at throwing a spear.

pages.title: A Long Journey
pages.content:
In Mahmud’s time, Arabic was the language of schools and books. But Mahmud loved his own language. “Turkish is great, too,” he thought.

In 1057, he started a long journey. For ten to fifteen years, he traveled from one Turkish tribe to another. He listened to the people and collected their words. He also wrote down their stories, songs and sayings. After that, he went to Baghdad and wrote his big book there.

vocabulary.definition: A long trip from one place to another.
A big group of families with one leader.
Words about things that happened.
A short, old sentence with a lesson.

pages.title: What Is in the Book?
pages.content:
The dictionary has about 9,000 Turkish words. It also has very old Turkish poems and sayings. You can find the names of many places and people in it, too. It even tells old stories from the Turkish world.

From this book, we can learn about the daily life of the Turks. What did they eat? What did they wear? What games did they play? The book is like a big window to Turkish culture.

The way of life of a group of people.

pages.title: A Problem with a Date
pages.content:
There is an old story about a calendar in the book.

A long time ago, there was a Turkish khan. He wanted to know the date of an old war. But nobody knew the right year. So the khan called all his people to a big meeting. This kind of meeting was a kurultay.

At the meeting, the khan said, “We can make a calendar. We can give a name to every year. Then we can find old dates.”

vocabulary.definition: A list of the days and months of a year.
An old Turkish king.
A big fight between two countries.

pages.title: Twelve Animals and a River
pages.content:
The people loved the khan’s idea, too, and they named the years in this way:

One day, the khan went hunting with his people. They pushed many wild animals to a big river in the Ili Valley. The water was fast and dangerous. Only twelve animals got to the other side.

The rat arrived first. So the first year is the Year of the Rat. Then come the Ox, the Leopard, the Rabbit and the Crocodile. After them come the Snake, the Horse, the Sheep and the Monkey. The last three are the Rooster, the Dog and the Pig. After the twelfth year, the Year of the Rat comes again.

vocabulary.definition: Can hurt you.

pages.title: A New Day
pages.content:
The old Turks thought about the animal of every year. The ox likes to fight with its horns. So they said, “There will be wars in the Year of the Ox.” Snakes and crocodiles live near water. So they said, “There will be a lot of rain in the Year of the Snake.”

For the old Turks, the new year started on March 21st. They had a big celebration on this day. Its name was Nowruz, and it means “new day”. Many people still celebrate Nowruz today.

vocabulary.definition: A big, strong male cow.
Hit and hurt another person or animal.
A hard, pointed thing on an animal's head.
A happy day with friends, food and music.

pages.title: The First Map with Japan
pages.content:
There is a map with many colors in Mahmud’s book. On it, the mountains are red, the seas are green, the rivers are blue, and the deserts are yellow. Balasagun, a city of the Turks, is in the middle of the map.

The map also shows Japan. It is the first world map with Japan on it! The next map with Japan came 400 years later. In 2024, UNESCO celebrated this great book. It is a real treasure of the Turkish language.

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
exercises.question: How does each verb show the past?
exercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed: start → started, travel → traveled. Some verbs change: write → wrote, give → gave, go → went, get → got.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: start, write … Does it add -ed or change?

exercises.title: Practise: In, On
exercises.question: Which word goes with the time?
exercises.explanation: In + year: in 1057. On + date: on March 21st.

feedback.incorrect: In 1057. On March 21st.

exercises.title: Practise: Is, Are
exercises.question: One or many?

formChoices.sentence: On the map, the mountains [choice] red.
Balasagun [choice] in the middle of the map.

exercises.explanation: One thing: is. Two or more: are.

feedback.incorrect: Mountains = many. Balasagun = one city.

exercises.title: Practise: Can and Will
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: Now or in the future?
exercises.fillBlanksText: “We [blank] make a calendar.” “There [blank] be wars in the Year of the Ox.” Many people [blank] celebrate Nowruz today.
exercises.explanation: Can + verb: it is possible. There will be: the future. Still = it did not stop.

feedback.incorrect: Find these words in Chapters 5 and 7.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Choose the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?

errorItems.sentence: Mahmud writed his book in Baghdad.
He gived the book to the Caliph.

exercises.explanation: “Write” and “give” change in the past: wrote, gave.

feedback.incorrect: Write → wrote. Give → gave. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: My Language
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about your language.
exercises.question: What is your language like?
exercises.explanation: Use is, like and means.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole story together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: The Dictionary
exercises.question: Which language did Mahmud use for his book?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “Mahmud wrote the book in Arabic.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Kashgar
exercises.question: Where is Kashgar?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “Kashgar is a very old city in East Turkestan.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: His Own Language
exercises.question: Mahmud loved his own language.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “But Mahmud loved his own language.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Which Animal?
exercises.instructions: Match the animal with the sentence.
exercises.question: Which animal is it?

matchingPairs.right: It likes to fight with its horns.

correctAnswer.the ox: It likes to fight with its horns.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: the rat. Chapter 7: the ox and the snake.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 6 and 7 again.

exercises.title: The Calendar
exercises.question: Why did the khan want a calendar?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “We can give a name to every year. Then we can find old dates.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: The River
exercises.question: All the animals got to the other side of the river.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “Only twelve animals got to the other side.”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is false. Only twelve animals got there.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: UNESCO
exercises.question: When did UNESCO celebrate this great book?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8: “In 2024, UNESCO celebrated this great book.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 8.

exercises.title: Mahmud’s Life and Book
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Mahmud gave his book to the Caliph.

exercises.explanation: Born in 1008 (Chapter 2) → the journey in 1057 (Chapter 3) → finished in 1074 → gave it to the Caliph in 1077 (Chapter 1).

feedback.correct: Great! You know Mahmud’s life and book.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the years: 1008, 1057, 1074, 1077.
